# The checks

<!-- purpose: What each check requires, where it applies, and which checks are only warnings -->

*This page is generated from SWCraft's own definitions, and describes the version you have installed.*

SWCraft checks a project every time it reads one. `swcraft check-model` runs every check below and writes nothing, which is what a build runs first; `swcraft validate` runs the same checks and, once every check that is an error has passed, generates the AUTOSAR file and checks that. So an error on this page never produces a file at all, while a file that fails the AUTOSAR check is left on disk to look at. The assistant runs them too, before it commits a change.

`rule:trace.requirement-unallocated` is a warning: listed by `check-model` and `validate`, never a refusal; `--warnings-as-errors` makes it one. `rule:trace.requirement-stub` is a warning: listed by `check-model` and `validate`, never a refusal; `--warnings-as-errors` makes it one. `rule:trace.link-version-not-stated` is a warning: listed by `check-model` and `validate`, never a refusal; `--warnings-as-errors` makes it one. `rule:trace.link-needs-confirmation` is a warning: listed by `check-model` and `validate`, never a refusal; `--warnings-as-errors` makes it one. `rule:trace.link-unpublishable-id` is a warning: listed by `check-model` and `validate`, never a refusal; `--warnings-as-errors` makes it one. `rule:trace.requirement-blank-text` is a warning: listed by `check-model` and `validate`, never a refusal; `--warnings-as-errors` makes it one. `rule:swc.variable.read-without-init` is a warning: listed by `check-model` and `validate`, never a refusal; `--warnings-as-errors` makes it one. Every other check is an error.

Each check has a name the product knows it by, one sentence saying what it requires, and the layers it reads. The sentence is the check's own: it is the same text SWCraft was built against.

## Checks on a single element { #checks-on-a-single-element }

<!-- purpose: Why one file is refused on its own: a value out of range, a blank name, an empty list -->

These read one file and need nothing else: a value outside its range, a name left blank, a list that has to hold at least one entry. They are reported as soon as the file is read, so they are the ones the editor and the assistant can answer immediately.

| Check | What it requires | Where it applies |

| `rule:implementation_types.implementation_element.type.not-blank`{ #implementation_types.implementation_element.type.not-blank } | An implementation record element's `type` must be non-blank. | [Implementation Types](model/implementation_types.md) |
| `rule:implementation_types.implementation_array.name.not-blank`{ #implementation_types.implementation_array.name.not-blank } | An implementation array's `name` must be non-blank and must not contain a path separator or a traversal segment. | [Implementation Types](model/implementation_types.md) |
| `rule:implementation_types.implementation_array.element_type.not-blank`{ #implementation_types.implementation_array.element_type.not-blank } | An implementation array's `element_type` must be non-blank. | [Implementation Types](model/implementation_types.md) |
| `rule:implementation_types.implementation_array.element_name.not-blank`{ #implementation_types.implementation_array.element_name.not-blank } | An implementation array's `element_name` must be non-blank. | [Implementation Types](model/implementation_types.md) |
| `rule:implementation_types.implementation_array.length.positive`{ #implementation_types.implementation_array.length.positive } | An implementation array's `length` must be greater than zero. | [Implementation Types](model/implementation_types.md) |
| `rule:implementation_types.pointer.name.not-blank`{ #implementation_types.pointer.name.not-blank } | A pointer's `name` must be non-blank and must not contain a path separator or a traversal segment. | [Implementation Types](model/implementation_types.md) |
| `rule:implementation_types.pointer.target-not-blank`{ #implementation_types.pointer.target-not-blank } | A pointer's `target` must be non-blank and different from its own `name`. | [Implementation Types](model/implementation_types.md) |
| `rule:application_types.range.bounds-coherent`{ #application_types.range.bounds-coherent } | A range's `min` must be less than or equal to its `max` where both are declared. | [Application Types](model/application_types.md) |
| `rule:application_types.conversion.limits-coherent`{ #application_types.conversion.limits-coherent } | A conversion's lower limit must not be above its upper one where both are declared, and the two may be equal only when both are closed. | [Application Types](model/application_types.md) |
| `rule:mapping_sets.mapping_set.name.not-blank`{ #mapping_sets.mapping_set.name.not-blank } | A mapping set's `name` must be non-blank and must not contain a path separator or a traversal segment. | [Mapping Sets](model/mapping_sets.md) |
| `rule:mapping_sets.mapping_set.maps.unique-application`{ #mapping_sets.mapping_set.maps.unique-application } | One application type may be paired at most once inside one mapping set. | [Mapping Sets](model/mapping_sets.md) |
| `rule:mapping_sets.map.reference-not-blank`{ #mapping_sets.map.reference-not-blank } | A pair's `application` and `implementation` must not be blank. | [Mapping Sets](model/mapping_sets.md) |
| `rule:swc.swc.data_type_mappings.no-duplicate-entry`{ #swc.swc.data_type_mappings.no-duplicate-entry } | A component must not name one mapping set twice, and no entry may be blank. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.port.com_specs.no-duplicate-entry`{ #swc.port.com_specs.no-duplicate-entry } | A port must not list the same `data_element` twice in `com_specs`. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.port_com_spec.alive_timeout.non-negative`{ #swc.port_com_spec.alive_timeout.non-negative } | A com-spec entry's `alive_timeout` must not be negative. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.port_com_spec.queue_length.positive`{ #swc.port_com_spec.queue_length.positive } | A com-spec entry's `queue_length` must be at least 1. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.disabled_mode.reference-form`{ #swc.disabled_mode.reference-form } | A disabled mode's `mode_group_ref` and `mode_ref` must each be an absolute ARXML path of identifier segments, the form an external stub's `external_ref` is held to. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:interfaces.data_element.calibration-access-supported`{ #interfaces.data_element.calibration-access-supported } | A data element whose `sw_impl_policy` is `queued` must not declare a `sw_calibration_access` of `read_only` or `read_write`: AUTOSAR supports no calibration access on a queued element. | [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md) |
| `rule:application_types.application_type.unit-form`{ #application_types.application_type.unit-form } | An application type states its unit inline (`unit`) or by reference (`unit_ref`), not both; a blank `unit` is none. | [Application Types](model/application_types.md) |
| `rule:application_types.application_type.conversion-form`{ #application_types.application_type.conversion-form } | An application type states its conversion inline (`conversion`) or by reference (`compu_method_ref`), not both. | [Application Types](model/application_types.md) |
| `rule:application_types.application_type.range-form`{ #application_types.application_type.range-form } | An application type states its range inline (`range`) or by reference (`data_constr_ref`), not both. | [Application Types](model/application_types.md) |
| `rule:application_types.enum.literals-form`{ #application_types.enum.literals-form } | An enumeration states exactly one of `literals` and `compu_method_ref`. | [Application Types](model/application_types.md) |
| `rule:application_types.application_type.unit_ref.not-blank`{ #application_types.application_type.unit_ref.not-blank } | An application type's `unit_ref`, where stated, must be non-blank. | [Application Types](model/application_types.md) |
| `rule:application_types.application_type.compu_method_ref.not-blank`{ #application_types.application_type.compu_method_ref.not-blank } | An application type's `compu_method_ref`, where stated, must be non-blank. | [Application Types](model/application_types.md) |
| `rule:application_types.application_type.data_constr_ref.not-blank`{ #application_types.application_type.data_constr_ref.not-blank } | An application type's `data_constr_ref`, where stated, must be non-blank. | [Application Types](model/application_types.md) |
| `rule:application_types.enum.compu_method_ref.not-blank`{ #application_types.enum.compu_method_ref.not-blank } | An enumeration's `compu_method_ref`, where stated, must be non-blank. | [Application Types](model/application_types.md) |
| `rule:implementation_types.value_type.compu_method_ref.not-blank`{ #implementation_types.value_type.compu_method_ref.not-blank } | A value type's `compu_method_ref`, where stated, must be non-blank. | [Implementation Types](model/implementation_types.md) |
| `rule:implementation_types.reference_type.compu_method_ref.not-blank`{ #implementation_types.reference_type.compu_method_ref.not-blank } | A reference type's `compu_method_ref`, where stated, must be non-blank. | [Implementation Types](model/implementation_types.md) |
| `rule:units.unit.name.not-blank`{ #units.unit.name.not-blank } | A unit's `name` must be non-blank and must not contain a path separator or a traversal segment. | [Units](model/units.md) |
| `rule:compu_methods.texttable.name.not-blank`{ #compu_methods.texttable.name.not-blank } | A texttable compu method's `name` must be non-blank and must not contain a path separator or a traversal segment. | [Compu Methods](model/compu_methods.md) |
| `rule:compu_methods.texttable.entries.not-empty`{ #compu_methods.texttable.entries.not-empty } | A texttable compu method must declare at least one entry. | [Compu Methods](model/compu_methods.md) |
| `rule:compu_methods.table_entry.name.not-blank`{ #compu_methods.table_entry.name.not-blank } | A table entry's `name` must be non-blank. | [Compu Methods](model/compu_methods.md) |
| `rule:compu_methods.linear.name.not-blank`{ #compu_methods.linear.name.not-blank } | A linear compu method's `name` must be non-blank and must not contain a path separator or a traversal segment. | [Compu Methods](model/compu_methods.md) |
| `rule:compu_methods.linear.unit.not-blank`{ #compu_methods.linear.unit.not-blank } | A linear compu method's `unit` must be non-blank. | [Compu Methods](model/compu_methods.md) |
| `rule:compu_methods.linear.limits-coherent`{ #compu_methods.linear.limits-coherent } | A linear compu method's lower limit must not be above its upper one where both are declared, and the two may be equal only when both are closed. | [Compu Methods](model/compu_methods.md) |
| `rule:data_constraints.data_constr.name.not-blank`{ #data_constraints.data_constr.name.not-blank } | A data constraint's `name` must be non-blank and must not contain a path separator or a traversal segment. | [Data Constraints](model/data_constraints.md) |
| `rule:data_constraints.data_constr.bounds-coherent`{ #data_constraints.data_constr.bounds-coherent } | A data constraint's `min` must be less than or equal to its `max` where both are declared. | [Data Constraints](model/data_constraints.md) |

## Checks between elements { #checks-between-elements }

<!-- purpose: Why elements disagree: a connector and its ports, a task and its runnables, a requirement link -->

These compare one element with another — a connector against the ports it names, a task against the runnables it schedules, a component's `satisfies` link against the requirement it names — so they are answered once the whole project has been read, and a project that is valid file by file can still fail here.

| Check | What it requires | Where it applies |
|---|---|---|
| `rule:trace.link-unknown-requirement`{ #trace.link-unknown-requirement } | A `satisfies` member naming no declared requirement, or carrying a version that is not one: a member is `<id>@<version>`, the version a positive integer, or the bare `<id>`. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Compositions](model/compositions.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md), [Tasks](model/tasks.md), [Hardware](model/hardware.md), [Requirements](model/requirements.md) |
| `rule:trace.requirement-unallocated`{ #trace.requirement-unallocated } | A requirement no `satisfies` member of any element names; a `derived_from` naming it is not an allocation. | [Requirements](model/requirements.md), [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Compositions](model/compositions.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md), [Tasks](model/tasks.md), [Hardware](model/hardware.md) |
| `rule:trace.requirement-stub`{ #trace.requirement-stub } | A requirement that is a stub: named as a parent and never imported. | [Requirements](model/requirements.md) |
| `rule:trace.link-version-not-stated`{ #trace.link-version-not-stated } | A `satisfies` or `derived_from` member naming a requirement by its bare `<id>`, with no `@<version>`. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Compositions](model/compositions.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md), [Tasks](model/tasks.md), [Hardware](model/hardware.md), [Requirements](model/requirements.md) |
| `rule:trace.link-needs-confirmation`{ #trace.link-needs-confirmation } | A `satisfies` or `derived_from` member whose `@<version>` is not the named requirement's current `version`. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Compositions](model/compositions.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md), [Tasks](model/tasks.md), [Hardware](model/hardware.md), [Requirements](model/requirements.md) |
| `rule:trace.derived-from-unknown-target`{ #trace.derived-from-unknown-target } | A `derived_from` member naming no declared requirement and no top-level element of a linkable layer, or carrying a version that is not one. | [Requirements](model/requirements.md), [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md), [Compositions](model/compositions.md), [Tasks](model/tasks.md), [Hardware](model/hardware.md) |
| `rule:trace.derived-from-cycle`{ #trace.derived-from-cycle } | Requirements deriving from each other, through `derived_from`, in a cycle. | [Requirements](model/requirements.md) |
| `rule:trace.decomposition-context-mismatch`{ #trace.decomposition-context-mismatch } | A decomposed requirement `X(Y)` whose `Y` is not the level before decomposition of a levelled requirement it derives from: that parent's own `(Y)` when it is decomposed, its level otherwise. | [Requirements](model/requirements.md) |
| `rule:trace.duplicate-link`{ #trace.duplicate-link } | One `satisfies` or `derived_from` list naming one target twice: a requirement, at the same version or at two, or one element; each list names a target once. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Compositions](model/compositions.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md), [Tasks](model/tasks.md), [Hardware](model/hardware.md), [Requirements](model/requirements.md) |
| `rule:trace.link-unpublishable-id`{ #trace.link-unpublishable-id } | A `satisfies` or `derived_from` member naming a requirement whose id holds `.`, which Sphinx-Needs reads as an id and a part: `generate needs` cannot publish the link. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Compositions](model/compositions.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md), [Tasks](model/tasks.md), [Hardware](model/hardware.md), [Requirements](model/requirements.md) |
| `rule:trace.requirement-blank-text`{ #trace.requirement-blank-text } | An architecture requirement whose `title` or `description` is empty or whitespace only: it is published, and the requirements import refuses it. | [Requirements](model/requirements.md) |
| `rule:connector.duplicate-name`{ #connector.duplicate-name } | Two connectors declaring the same name. | [Connectors](model/connectors.md) |
| `rule:connector.duplicate-link`{ #connector.duplicate-link } | Two connectors declaring the same endpoint pair. | [Connectors](model/connectors.md) |
| `rule:connector.endpoint-unknown-swc`{ #connector.endpoint-unknown-swc } | A connector endpoint naming no declared SWC. | [Connectors](model/connectors.md), [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:connector.endpoint-unknown-port`{ #connector.endpoint-unknown-port } | A connector endpoint naming a port that component does not declare. | [Connectors](model/connectors.md), [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Compositions](model/compositions.md) |
| `rule:connector.from-not-provide`{ #connector.from-not-provide } | A connector's `from` endpoint is not a provide port. | [Connectors](model/connectors.md), [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Compositions](model/compositions.md) |
| `rule:connector.to-not-require`{ #connector.to-not-require } | A connector's `to` endpoint is not a require port. | [Connectors](model/connectors.md), [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Compositions](model/compositions.md) |
| `rule:connector.interface-mismatch`{ #connector.interface-mismatch } | A connector whose required port's interface is not satisfied by the provided port's: a kind that differs (an external interface stub's kind is the one its `external_dest` names), a data element or operation without a counterpart of the same name, or a counterpart whose resolved type or signature differs, a data element queued on one side only, or an `is_service` that differs. Not judged: an external interface stub beyond its kind, or whose `external_dest` is abstract; invalidValue, a value type's own unit and range, interface mappings. | [Connectors](model/connectors.md), [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Compositions](model/compositions.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md), [Base Types](model/base_types.md), [Implementation Types](model/implementation_types.md), [Application Types](model/application_types.md) |
| `rule:connector.pointer-between-application-components`{ #connector.pointer-between-application-components } | A connector whose two ends are application components, followed through delegations across nested compositions, and whose interface carries a data element or an argument typed by a pointer, directly or through reference types: a pointer crosses a port only where one end is a service or an ECU-abstraction component. Not judged: an end that is an external component stub or that no delegation resolves to a component, and a pointer inside an implementation record or array. | [Connectors](model/connectors.md), [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Compositions](model/compositions.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md), [Implementation Types](model/implementation_types.md) |
| `rule:connector.endpoint-unknown-composition`{ #connector.endpoint-unknown-composition } | A connector endpoint naming no declared composition. | [Connectors](model/connectors.md), [Compositions](model/compositions.md) |
| `rule:connector.unknown-composition`{ #connector.unknown-composition } | A connector naming no declared composition. | [Connectors](model/connectors.md), [Compositions](model/compositions.md) |
| `rule:port.undeclared-interface`{ #port.undeclared-interface } | A port of a component that is not an external stub naming no declared interface, or none at all (an external interface stub counts as declared). | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md) |
| `rule:swc.access.unknown-port`{ #swc.access.unknown-port } | A runnable access naming a port its component does not declare. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.access.unknown-element`{ #swc.access.unknown-element } | A runnable read or write naming no data element of the port's sender/receiver interface, or, through a port on an external interface stub, no name the stub lists in its `data_elements`. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md) |
| `rule:swc.access.unknown-operation`{ #swc.access.unknown-operation } | A runnable call naming no operation of the port's client/server interface, or, through a port on an external interface stub, no name the stub lists in its `operations`. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md) |
| `rule:swc.access.direction-mismatch`{ #swc.access.direction-mismatch } | A read or call through a provide port, or a write through a require port. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.access.interface-kind-mismatch`{ #swc.access.interface-kind-mismatch } | A read or write through a client/server port, or a call through a sender/receiver port. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md) |
| `rule:swc.operation-event.unknown-port`{ #swc.operation-event.unknown-port } | An operation event naming a port its component does not declare. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.operation-event.direction-mismatch`{ #swc.operation-event.direction-mismatch } | An operation event through a require port. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.operation-event.interface-kind-mismatch`{ #swc.operation-event.interface-kind-mismatch } | An operation event through a port whose interface is sender/receiver. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md) |
| `rule:swc.operation-event.unknown-operation`{ #swc.operation-event.unknown-operation } | An operation event naming no operation of the port's client/server interface, or, through a port on an external interface stub, no name the stub lists in its `operations`. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md) |
| `rule:swc.operation-event.duplicate-binding`{ #swc.operation-event.duplicate-binding } | A `(port, operation)` pair named by more than one operation event of one component, on two runnables or twice on one. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.operation-event.incompatible-signatures`{ #swc.operation-event.incompatible-signatures } | A runnable started by operation events whose operations differ in argument count, in an argument's direction, or in the structure of an argument's resolved implementation type, position by position. Not judged: a position whose type does not resolve completely, or whose application type or enumeration the component's mapping sets do not map to exactly one implementation type; possible errors, the return value, errorHandling, serverArgumentImplPolicy and PortDefinedArgumentValues. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md), [Mapping Sets](model/mapping_sets.md), [Application Types](model/application_types.md), [Implementation Types](model/implementation_types.md) |
| `rule:swc.external-with-ports`{ #swc.external-with-ports } | An external stub component declaring a port with an interface, measures or com-specs, runnables, variables, exclusive areas, a memory budget, data type mappings, a termination and restart handling, a package or a behaviour name. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.external-incomplete-reference`{ #swc.external-incomplete-reference } | An external stub with a blank or malformed `external_ref`/`external_dest`. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.external-reference-without-stub`{ #swc.external-reference-without-stub } | A component declaring `external_ref` or `external_dest` without `external: true`. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.external-reference-inside-generated-package`{ #swc.external-reference-inside-generated-package } | An external stub whose `external_ref` lies inside a package the generated ARXML declares the project's own elements in. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.undeclared-termination-and-restart`{ #swc.undeclared-termination-and-restart } | A component whose behaviour is emitted and that sets no `handle_termination_and_restart`, which AUTOSAR 4.2.2 and 4.3.0 require on every behaviour. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.port.com-spec-unknown-element`{ #swc.port.com-spec-unknown-element } | A port's `com_specs` entry naming no data element of the port's sender/receiver interface or, on a port typed by an external interface stub, no name the stub lists in its `data_elements`, or any entry on a port whose interface is client/server or undeclared. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md) |
| `rule:swc.port.com-spec-inapplicable`{ #swc.port.com-spec-inapplicable } | A port's `com_specs` entry stating an attribute with no place on the port's side or the element's policy: a receiver-only attribute on a provide port, `queue_length` on an element that is not queued, a non-queued receiver attribute on a queued element, or an `init` on a queued element. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md) |
| `rule:swc.port.com-spec-on-stub`{ #swc.port.com-spec-on-stub } | A port's `com_specs` entry for a data element an external interface stub lists that states an `init`, which the stub holds no type to shape, or, on a require port, a `queue_length`, since the com-spec of a stub's member is never queued. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md) |
| `rule:swc.port.queued-receiver-without-queue-length`{ #swc.port.queued-receiver-without-queue-length } | A component's require port whose interface declares a queued data element and whose `com_specs` give that element no `queue_length`, which a queued receiver com-spec carries and nothing defaults. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md) |
| `rule:swc.timing_event.disabled-mode-port`{ #swc.timing_event.disabled-mode-port } | An event's disabled mode whose `port` is not a require port of the component typed by an external interface stub with `external_dest` MODE-SWITCH-INTERFACE, or whose `mode_group_ref` does not lie directly under that stub's `external_ref`. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md) |
| `rule:swc.access.queued-read-by-value`{ #swc.access.queued-read-by-value } | A runnable reading a queued data element `by: value`. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md) |
| `rule:swc.variable.undeclared-type`{ #swc.variable.undeclared-type } | A component's variable whose `application_type` names no declared application type, or whose `implementation_type` names no declared implementation type (an external data type stub counts as declared). | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Application Types](model/application_types.md), [Implementation Types](model/implementation_types.md) |
| `rule:swc.variable-access.unknown-variable`{ #swc.variable-access.unknown-variable } | A runnable's variable access naming no variable of its own component. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.variable.pointer-type`{ #swc.variable.pointer-type } | A component's variable typed by a pointer — named directly, at the end of a chain of reference types, or, for an application type, through the implementation type the component's mapping sets pair it with. A variable whose application type no set or more than one set pairs, or whose type is an external data type stub, is not judged. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Implementation Types](model/implementation_types.md), [Mapping Sets](model/mapping_sets.md) |
| `rule:swc.variable.read-without-init`{ #swc.variable.read-without-init } | A variable that a runnable of its component reads and that states no `init`: AUTOSAR leaves the value undefined when the read comes before every write, and the model states no order of execution, so no write can be shown to come first. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.exclusive-area.unknown-area`{ #swc.exclusive-area.unknown-area } | A runnable's `can_enter` or `runs_inside` entry naming no exclusive area of its own component. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.data-event.unknown-port`{ #swc.data-event.unknown-port } | A data-received event naming a port its component does not declare. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.data-event.direction-mismatch`{ #swc.data-event.direction-mismatch } | A data-received event through a provide port. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |
| `rule:swc.data-event.interface-kind-mismatch`{ #swc.data-event.interface-kind-mismatch } | A data-received event through a port whose interface is client/server, or an external interface stub whose `external_dest` is not SENDER-RECEIVER-INTERFACE. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md) |
| `rule:swc.data-event.unknown-element`{ #swc.data-event.unknown-element } | A data-received event naming no data element of the port's sender/receiver interface, or, through a port on an external interface stub, no name the stub lists in its `data_elements`. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md) |
| `rule:swc.access.queued-implicit-read`{ #swc.access.queued-implicit-read } | A runnable reading a queued data element `by: implicit`: an implicit read takes one value before the runnable starts, and a queued element has no one value to take. | [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Interfaces](model/interfaces.md) |
| `rule:swc.access.implicit-read-enable-update`{ #swc.access.implicit-read-enable-update } | A runnable reading `by: implicit` a data element its port's `com_specs` entry states `enable_update: true` for. | [SWCs](model/swc.md) |

## Checks on a kind of value { #checks-on-a-kind-of-value }

<!-- purpose: The checks that hold for a kind of value wherever it appears, across layers -->

These are not about one layer. They hold wherever the kind of value they describe appears, which is why one of them can list fields from several layers at once.

| Check | What it requires | Where it applies |
|---|---|---|
| `rule:model.float-finite`{ #model.float-finite } | No float field of any element may hold `.nan`, `.inf` or `-.inf`. | [Application Types](model/application_types.md), [Implementation Types](model/implementation_types.md), [Compu Methods](model/compu_methods.md), [Data Constraints](model/data_constraints.md), [Hardware](model/hardware.md), [SWCs](model/swc.md), [Tasks](model/tasks.md) |
